newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis steady-firm as CBOT slides.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis steady-firm as CBOT slides.

text.p: Sharply lower trading in CBOT soymeal futures was overshadowing activity in cash soymeal markets Friday, U.S. Midwestern soymeal brokers said.
"There's not really anything going on here," one broker said. "We're all just standing around looking at the (CBOT price) board."
Offers for soymeal by truck were mixed, but a smattering of export business was firming up CIF and FOB quotes, brokers said. Offers for meal by rail were steady to higher.
"We're up slightly on a little business to China," one dealer said.
The sharply lower futures could prompt some elevators to "let go of some grain and get it moving to the processors," one broker said.

Some cash sources were expecting a weekend of good harvest weather in most of the Midwest to spur activity in the market next week. Private forecasters were calling for warmer, drier weather throughout the corn belt
Brokers noted that a greater-than-expected weekly crush rate could generate supply pressure. NOPA put the crush at 25.62 million bushels, up from 23.52 million a week ago.
